title: Automated purge orchestration for ephemeral KV and model-context stores with tamper-evident proof
creator: Lydia Chen
description:
Problem: Redwood runs several ephemeral state stores during inference (KV caches, conversation context shards, temporary embeddings caches and derived feature stores). These can contain customer data or customer-identifiable context and are not always covered by our long-lived deletion workflows because they live outside the primary data lake. Compliance teams require automated, verifiable deletion across these ephemeral stores when a tenant requests RTBF or when retention rules trigger.

Goal: Implement a policy-driven orchestration layer that can target ephemeral stores, stage and execute selective purges, and emit a tamper-evident proof bundle (signed log + cryptographic checksums) that can be exported to customers and retained in internal audit storage. The system should support scheduled retention enforcement, tenant-initiated RTBF, and be compatible with Dedicated/Private deployments where possible.
acceptance_criteria: Define a retention-rule mapping that can reference ephemeral store types (KV-cache, model-context, embedding-temp) and tenant scopes
Create an orchestrator that can perform staged purge operations: mark->drain->verify->compact, with idempotent retries
Produce a signed proof bundle for each purge that contains: immutable event log (timestamped), checksums of affected shards, operation outcome, and operator metadata
Expose an API endpoint for tenants to request RTBF that returns a job ID and, on completion, a downloadable proof bundle URL
Provide dashboard traces and per-tenant audit entries visible in Console release console-2026.04
Ensure the flow respects geofencing: data in region X must be purged by region-local agents and proof bundles are region-stamped
technical_considerations: Ephemeral stores may be replicated or cached in hardware local memory — need safe drain semantics to avoid partial deletes causing corrupt model state
Must define canonical identifiers for ephemeral shards so proofs can refer to stable objects even if storage backends recycle names
Cryptographic proof format should be compact (JSON-LD + detached signature) and compatible with customer archival systems
Performance: purge operations must be rate-limited and backoff-aware to avoid disrupting serving SLOs; provide a burst window option for emergency RTBF
Compatibility with Private deployments: orchestrator should be distributable as an operator/controller with config toggles for on-prem KMS and audit sinks
runbook_steps: PM triages request and creates a tenant-scoped purge job via Console or API
Orchestrator marks target shards as 'pending-purge' and signals serving runtime to route new requests away
Serving runtime drains live in-memory caches by migrating KV state to ephemeral tombstone store
Orchestrator issues delete on underlying stores, computes checksums pre/post-delete, and stores signed proof records in audit-store
Post-delete verification runs cross-checks (list vs expected ids) and flags any mismatches for manual review
On success, proof bundle is generated, signed with platform key, region-stamped, and attached to tenant export endpoint
dependencies: ENG-22891 (serving: drain hook for eviction-aware KV migration)
ENG-24105 (audit-store: append-only ledger + signing key rotation support)
ENG-25518 (console: per-tenant job UI and proof download)
comments: 2026-03-11 | Lydia Chen (PM): Initial scoping complete — prioritized P1 due to upcoming EMEA customer audit. Assigned to Miguel for technical feasibility spike.

2026-03-12 | Miguel Ortega (ENG): Spike performed — drain hook can be added to runtime but will require coordination with autotuner. Estimate increased from 5 to 8 points for discovery and backwards compatibility.
2026-03-13 | Asha Patel (Security): Suggest using detached JWS signatures and a dedicated key per-region with rotation policy. Will schedule security review once design doc is published.
2026-03-14 | Lydia Chen (PM): Added requirement for exportable bundle URL and region stamping. Note: need legal input on proof retention duration (default 90 days).
notes: Consider providing a 'dry-run' mode where proofs show intended deletions and checksums without performing destructive operations — useful for customer attestation before actual RTBF
Allow customers to opt-in for extended proof retention (archival to S3 with encryption and custom retention tags)
For Dedicated customers, include a knob to route proofs to customer-managed audit sinks (SFTP/HTTP webhook)
